prerequisites.title: X developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign in at console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and describe how you will use the API.

prerequisites.title: Prepaid API credits
prerequisites.detail: Usage is billed per call from credits bought upfront; calls are blocked when the balance goes negative.

prerequisites.title: X representative for Ads API
prerequisites.detail: Raising Ads API access or the user token limit goes through an X representative.

steps.title: Create developer account
steps.detail: Sign in, accept the agreement and give basic use information. Be specific about the use case.

steps.title: Wait for developer approval if asked
steps.detail: One report says approval ranges from immediate to several days. It comes from a competitor's blog.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click New App and enter a name, description and use case.

steps.title: Save OAuth 2.0 client ID and secret
steps.detail: Credentials show only once. Store them securely right away.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Choose only the scopes the agent needs; the consent screen shows exactly those.

steps.title: Register callback URL
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it to the app's settings in the X console.
steps.done_when: Callback URL saved in app settings

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Buy credits and set spend limit
steps.detail: Buy credits in the Developer Console and set a per-cycle spending cap.

steps.title: Contact your X representative
steps.detail: Ask to apply for Standard Access for the Ads API.

traps.title: The page describes per-app limits (Bearer Token, app-only) and
traps.detail: The page describes per-app limits (Bearer Token, app-only) and per-user limits (OAuth 1.0a or OAuth 2.0 user tokens) but does not tie either to app review status.

traps.title: Credentials are shown only once
traps.detail: Losing them means regenerating, which invalidates the old ones.

traps.title: Costs accrue per call
traps.detail: Post creation costs $0.015 per request and post reads $0.005 per resource. Pay-per-usage plans cap at 3 million Post reads per cycle.

traps.title: Vague use case may be rejected
traps.detail: One report lists vague use-case text as a common rejection cause.

traps.title: Rate limits are not raised for Ads
traps.detail: X does not increase rate limits for any Ads API endpoint.

blockers.what_it_means: A per-endpoint rate limit was exceeded until the window resets.

blockers.what_it_means: The balance went negative or the spend cap was reached.
blockers.what_to_do: Add credits or wait for the next billing cycle.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so the developer does not need to register an OAuth app or supply a client ID and secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If `composio_managed_auth_schemes` contains the toolkit's OAuth method, Composio provides the OAuth app. If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.question: C1
